Photo to vinyl
Pick a photo and VinylStudio turns it into cut sheets, one per vinyl color. Work left to right: Prepare, Styles, Adjust, Colors, Layers, Export.
No photo yet? Tap Try sample photo to practice.
1. Prepare your photo
Import and Crop your photo. To remove the background, place Snip points, tap Close points, then Apply snip. Adjust Lighting, then Size.
Pinch to zoom before placing Snip points. Sharp, evenly lit photos work best.
2. Pick and tune a style
Open Styles to choose a rendering family. In Adjust, change density, spacing or detail. Change one slider at a time and wait for the final render.
Small art? Choose bold, connected shapes. More density is not always more detail.
3. Choose colors and layers
In Colors, pick your background and the vinyl colors you own. In Layers, check each sheet. Upper vinyl covers what is below it.
Pick colors with strong light-to-dark contrast. Eight colors do not guarantee eight populated cut layers.
4. Export and cut
In Export, check Boundary and Marks. Pick Output and export the cut ZIP (or PDF for a printer). For vinyl, export the assembly guide PDF.
Always make a test cut on scrap vinyl first. The app makes files; it does not run the cutter.
Face looks lost?
Compare the photo in Prepare with the result. If eyes or mouth vanish, adjust Lighting in Prepare, pick colors further apart, or check which layer covers them.
Judge the portrait from normal viewing distance, not zoomed in.
Too many colors?
Lower the layer count in Colors or Layers. Supported styles try to keep useful colors. Similar colors add cutting work without improving the picture.
Keep one dark, one middle and one light vinyl, then add more only if needed.
Will it fit my mat?
On a 12 × 12 mat the app checks an 11.5-inch usable span. Height, padding and marks all count, so aim for about 11 inches or less.
At 3–4 inches use fewer colors and bigger shapes. Never shrink one sheet on its own.
Preview looks wrong or slow?
Let go of the slider and wait for the final render. Tap Show controls if the canvas is full screen. Lower density if rendering is slow.
If Export says Final render pending, wait. Still stuck? Save, then use Copy last crash report.
Line styles
Adjust line spacing and coverage together. Use Light-area lines to keep detail in bright spots. Fine-line styles need enough size to cut cleanly.
Lines disappearing? Lower density before lowering the minimum cut width.
Shape, cell and camo styles
Bigger dots and tiles cut and weed easier. Cell styles offer Motif family and Cell density. Fish Scale has a Raised edge accent sheet toggle.
Tiny pieces vanish or tear? Use fewer cells. Digital Camo squares are on purpose.
Lining up the layers
In Export → Marks, place the four marks outside the art. Every sheet gets them in the same spot, so you can stack layers by matching marks.
These are manual alignment marks, not Print Then Cut sensor marks.
Cutting with Cricut
Choose Cricut under Output and unzip the cut ZIP. Upload each SVG at its real size. Attach the art and marks so they stay in place on the mat.
Measure the imported art in Design Space before cutting the full job.
Silhouette and other cutters
Silhouette Basic: DXF; check the 100 mm square and dimensions-dxf.txt. Other cutters: SVG; Brother converts to FCM in CanvasWorkspace. Follow ZIP notes.
Printers: composite PDF at 100%, not Print Then Cut. Set cutter material in cutter software.
Weed, stack and apply
Cut, weed the extra vinyl, then lift with transfer tape. Apply the bottom sheet first and stack upward, lining up the marks. Peel the marks off at the end.
Heat-transfer vinyl has different rules. Follow the maker and test on scrap.
Save and back up
Use Save to library often, and Save as new project before big changes. Export project ZIP makes an editable backup. A cut ZIP cannot be reopened for editing.
Keep the project ZIP with your cut sheets and assembly guide.

Privacy & About
VinylStudio · Privacy & About
Open public privacy policy

VinylStudio is an offline-first design editor. Imported photos, artwork, project archives, palettes, settings and local Java crash diagnostics are processed and stored on this device. The application does not include analytics, advertisements or an automatic data-upload service.
You control exports and backups. When you choose a destination such as a file provider, cloud storage or another cutting application, that destination may process the files under its own privacy policy.
Local files remain on the device until you delete them or clear the application data. Backup exports are controlled by you. Uninstalling or clearing application storage can permanently delete local projects.
The public privacy policy contains contact details and the complete data-handling statement.
